proof_summary: At \(n=5\), the bounds \(8/7<\sqrt2<10/7\) give \(a(4)=3\) and \(a(5)=4\), so the difference is \(1\). But \(5\neq\lfloor k\phi\rfloor\) for every \(k\ge1\): the first three floors are \(1,3,4\), while for \(k\ge4\) the floor is at least \(6\), contradicting the asserted characterization of difference-one positions.
